narrative.managementWorld: a quiet architect's drawing of the home
narrative.overview:
HomeyDash has two faces. A display is a wall of soft, button-like tiles, read across a room and touched for a second. Management is **"a quiet architect's drawing of the home"**: a pale blue-grey sheet with white panels drawn in hairlines, small letter-spaced plan labels heading each block, and one hue per part of the home on its marks, so you can tell where you are at a glance. Colour on a display belongs to the thing being controlled: every tile kind owns one hue, and nothing else on a display is coloured. Colour in Management belongs to the place you are in; actions keep one ink-blue.

Displays are calm. Nothing moves on its own except a photo fading to the next and a Plex progress bar. When left alone a display turns into a photo frame with a quiet layer of white lock-screen widgets over the picture.

Management is visited every few weeks by someone who does not remember where things live, so its frame never changes: the same five places, in the same order and colours, with what is in each. Displays are drawn as framed screen outlines; the editor's stage still shows the real tiles exactly as a display does.

The system follows the device's light or dark preference, and never hard-codes one theme.
keyCharacteristics: Colour means a kind of thing; status colour is only ever status.
Tiles feel like buttons: one soft lift, controls inside sit flat, a press shrinks the tile.
Everything on a display scales from one `--cell`, the screen height divided by the row count (4 by default).
Management is drawn, not lifted: hairlines, plan labels, a place hue for where you are, one ink-blue for what you can do.
Plain English, sentence case, no emoji or exclamation marks.

rules.name: The Kind Hue Rule
rules.body: A resting tile carries a light tint of its kind (22% fill over the surface); an active tile fills with it. Inactive tiles stay on `tile-surface` with a tinted icon, so a dashboard is still colourful when everything is off. The share is `--rest-tint`: 22% in light, 36% in dark, where the fills are deep and 22% left heat, security, climate and cover tiles the same grey-blue. Poster and cover art dims to 70% brightness in dark (`--art-dim`), so it is not the brightest thing on a night wall.

rules.name: The Status Is Never Decoration Rule
rules.body: `ok`, `warn` and `danger` appear only with a word; colour alone never carries state.

rules.name: The Brand Stays In Management Rule
rules.body: `brand` never appears on a display tile.

rules.name: The Where You Are Rule
rules.body: A place hue says where you are: the mark beside a place and a page title, the legend key beside a row, the current item in the sidebar, the hover wash of a row and the selected hit in Go to. It never fills a button, colours a link, or draws a focus ring.

rules.name: The One Action Colour Rule
rules.body: Everything you can do in Management is `mgmt-brand`: primary buttons, links, selection, focus. A second accent for actions is never added.

rules.name: The Distinct From Warn Rule
rules.body: No place hue may read as a status colour. Accounts is plum, not amber, because `warn` is amber; a new place gets a hue clear of `ok`, `warn` and `danger`.

rules.name: The Cell Scales Type Rule
rules.body: Never use fixed pixels for type on a display, except the 44px minimum on touch controls, the screen title and touch input roles, and the `--text-floor`.

rules.name: The Line Break Rule
rules.body: Headings and tile names use `text-wrap: balance`; lines of prose (lead, hint, muted) use `text-wrap: pretty`.

rules.name: The Plan Label Rule
rules.body: A plan label is the heading of its block, never a line set above another heading.

rules.name: The Press Rule
rules.body: A pressed tile scales to 0.96 and darkens slightly. Every pressable surface also shows a ripple from the point of the press.

rules.name: The Tinted Not Raised Rule
rules.body: Controls (slider track, segmented control, round buttons) are the kind ink at low opacity, never raised. The tile's quick action is the one solid control.

rules.name: The Drawn Not Lifted Rule
rules.body: In Management, depth is a hairline. A shadow means a modal dialog is open over the page.

dos: Do give every new tile kind one hue pair, 4.5:1 ink on `tile-surface`, and use `ink` on its fill.
Do size everything on a display from `--cell`, keeping 44px as the touch minimum.
Do write in the domain language: Dashboard, Display, Tile, Section, Publish, Draft, Photo set, Account.
Do respect `prefers-reduced-motion`; drop press transitions and slow spinners.
Do set `--sec` on everything that belongs to a place, and open every Management page with the page header: crumbs, mark, title, purpose line, actions.
Do keep the five places in the same order, with the same hues, on every page.
Do head a Management block with a plan label (11px/600, 0.1em, uppercase) and divide its rows with 1px `mgmt-line` hairlines.
donts: Don't recolour a tile for its state. Intensity changes; the hue doesn't. State colour goes on elements inside the tile.
Don't use `brand` on a display tile, or status colours as decoration.
Don't add shadows to Management outside its modal dialogs, or inside a tile.
Don't put a place hue on a button, a link or a focus ring; actions are `mgmt-brand` only.
Don't give a place a hue that can be read as `ok`, `warn` or `danger`.
Don't restyle the editor stage to match Management.
Don't use emoji, exclamation marks, or "please" in copy.
Don't move or reflow tiles on their own; nothing animates except photos and Plex progress.
